question.problem: Find the principal axes of the curve $5{x}_{1}^{2}+24{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2}=52.$
question.worked_solution:
First, consider the quadratic form $Q(x)=5{x}_{1}^{2}+24{x}_{1}{x}_{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2}.$ The matrix of the form is

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 12 \\ 12 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that $A$ is symmetric. The principal axes of the curve 

$$
{x}^{T}\,Ax=52
$$

are the vectors that form an orthonormal eigenvector basis of $A.$ 

By solving the characteristic equation $|A-\lambda I|=0,$ we obtain

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=13\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-13.$

Let's now find the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=13,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-13I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 12 \\ 12 & -5\end{aligned}]-13[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 12 \\ 12 & -18\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-13I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{1}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{1}‖=\sqrt{13},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-13,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-13)I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 12 \\ 12 & -5\end{aligned}]+13[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}18 & 12 \\ 12 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-13I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{13},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

$\,$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
